## 2026-11-03T22:50Z Independent review findings corrected

- An independent read-only reviewer examined the full diff. It found one critical, two high, five medium and several low issues; authorization/identity had no exploitable defect.
- Critical: HTTP ingest passed the default privacy policy (`allowSourceText=false`), so every visible model output was silently rewritten to "withheld (unsupported)" before storage. E2E asserted only event kinds, so it stayed green. Fixed with an ingest policy that permits already-scrubbed source text; the E2E now asserts the exact visible text survives producer → signed ingest → SQL → authorized read.
- High: the producer's ref'd heartbeat timer prevented Node scripts from exiting, so enabling the feature could hang `generate-site-config`. Periodic timers are now unref'd; a spawned Node regression proves a script exits without an explicit close.
- High: forward catch-up selected the newest rows above the cursor, so a burst over 100 events could skip the middle. SQL now reads oldest-first for `after`, the store preserves direction, and a 150-event real-PostgreSQL test proves no gap across two pages.
- Medium fixes: expired partitions are served as expired rather than healthy; retention now runs before and independently of the lifecycle reconciliation mode; contact-shaped values are redacted from error messages and labels without stripping public contact copy from model output; the stage rail keeps unfinished stages active instead of "done"; disabling the feature removes the section entirely; permanent SQL rejections map to 400/403/409 so producers stop retrying; `close()` judges completeness after attempted delivery; heartbeat warnings use server `observedAt`; older paging is bounded; the coverage inventory now has a CI-checked contract test.
- Remaining documented limits: rendering/repair/imagery/preview actions stay limited or unsupported in the inventory; the browser suite renders a synthetic contract-valid trace (the real producer is proven separately through ingest, SQL and the read route); a full parent run must still prove the finalizer live.
- Verification after fixes: contract 18/18, client 15/15, context 7/7, format 8/8, model and pipeline suites pass, PostgreSQL activity 11/11, E2E 3/3, Worker activity 30/30, activity browser subset 4/4. Full browser and full suites were rerun afterward; results are recorded in the completion entry.

## 19:16 UTC - Focus-state contrast false positives fixed

- Task: Work OS `a76347aa-b800-4a71-b150-a5a7e765071d`.
- Commit `f7352523`; deploy `41700475093` succeeded on that SHA.
- Root cause: interaction states re-collected every text target, but
  `resolveRenderedBackdrop` skipped all out-of-scope targets. A focus or scroll
  revealed painted layer could newly overlap an untouched heading, leaving the
  new overlap issue unresolved and failing the page even though the heading's
  default state was clean.
- Fix: keep a default-state target map. When a previously clean target becomes
  unresolved in an interaction state, mark it for a rendered-pixel proof and
  bypass the scope skip for that target only. Targets already unresolved in
  the default state remain fail-closed.
- Validation: the new positive and fail-closed tests pass; 128 contrast tests
  pass across six files with a 30 second timeout while the host was under heavy
  load; `npm run check` reports 0 errors and 0 warnings across 501 files.
- Real-candidate proof: on the selected Alder & Iron service page the old
  module produced exactly one unresolved focus finding for "What is happening,
  and what comes next"; the fixed module produced zero findings and passed.
- The full default-timeout suite was not a usable signal while the host load
  average was above 30: 87 unrelated browser tests hit their 5 second timeout.
  The same two suites fail harder on the pre-fix module, so this is
  environmental, not a regression from the change.
- Next: wire focused-run thumbnail tracking and remove the hollow services
  panel and empty FAQ frame before the next plumbing run.
